Welcome to Digging for Dinos, where adventure, discovery, and competition collide! As a team of daring paleontologists, you’ll explore dig sites, unearth ancient fossils, and race against rival teams to assemble the most complete dinosaurs. Every move counts as you compete to claim the rarest finds and piece together prehistoric giants. With simple yet strategic gameplay, Digging for Dinos is perfect for families, friends, and fossil fanatics of all ages. Grab your tools, out- dig the competition, and bring history to life—one fossil at a time! Players control 2 paleontologists. Each turn they move one to a new dig site card, collecting the card from where they moved. Each card represents a section of a dinosaur fossil. Collect all the fossils needed to complete a specific dinosaur to score more points at the end of the game. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Goal 2 Turn Overview 3 Movement 4 Flip the Paleontologist 5 Collecting Fossils 6 Completing Dinosaurs 7 Special Ability 8 End Game 9 Scoring 10 Winning Goal Collect fossil tiles and complete dinosaur skeletons to score the most points. The player with the highest score at the end of the game wins. Turn Overview Players take turns clockwise. On your turn: Move one of your paleontologists Flip that paleontologist Collect the fossil tile you moved from Replace the tile with a new one from the current era Movement Move a Paleontologist Choose one of your two paleontologists and move it in the direction shown on the token. Each token has two sides: Orthogonal side – move up, down, left, or right Diagonal side – move diagonally Movement Rules You must move in one of the directions shown on the token. You cannot land on a space occupied by another paleontologist. You may jump over any number of tokens to reach the next open tile in that direction. You cannot move off the board. If no legal move is available, move one of your tokens to any open tile , ignoring movement rules. Flip the Paleontologist After moving, flip the paleontologist token to its other side . This causes the paleontologist to alternate between: Orthogonal movement Diagonal movement Collecting Fossils After moving: Take the fossil tile you moved from and place it in front of you. Replace that tile with a new fossil tile from the current era stack . If the current era stack is empty, begin drawing tiles from the next era . Completing Dinosaurs Fossil tiles belong to dinosaur sets. Each tile shows: The dinosaur species Its position in the skeleton Two scoring values: - Left number – points if the dinosaur is incomplete - Right number – points if the dinosaur is completed To complete a dinosaur, collect all tiles in its set . Special Ability Completing either of the following dinosaurs triggers an ability: Velociraptor Deinosuchus When one of these dinosaurs is completed, the player may immediately flip one of their paleontologist tokens . End Game The game ends when either condition occurs: 1 - The final Era 3 fossil tile is placed on the board. or 2 - A player completes their fourth dinosaur . All players finish the current round so everyone has taken the same number of turns. At the end of the round, players will collect the fossil tiles that their paleontologist tokens are currently on. Scoring Players score their fossil tiles as follows: Incomplete dinosaurs: score the left value on each fossil tile Completed dinosaurs: score the right value once for the entire set Tiles in completed dinosaurs do not score individually . Winning The player with the most points wins . Tiebreaker If players are tied: Compare the largest scoring completed dinosaur If still tied, compare the next largest Continue until the tie is broken Board Game Arena would like to thank Th3rd World Studios for making it possible to have this game here. 2634 diggingfordinos العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti

[Rating: 4/10] Played on BGA. Completed the 4th Dino to end the game, had my archaeolgist on a tile to complete my 5th, opponent only completed 3, we tied in points but I lost because he completed a triceratops which was the highest scoring completed Dino and is the tiebreaker. Kinda dumb tiebreaker and seems like should be the second tiebreaking step to determine the winner after most completed Dinos but whatever. I liked it until the sour taste in my mouth of the tiebreaking ending. Kinda removes the incentive to complete Dinos and you might as well just go for 4 point tiles and the triceratops for tiebrea
